France had an unexpectedly high turnout, estimated to be over 50% - the highest in decades - and higher than the last parliamentary elections.

From noon on Sunday, as voters went to the polls, it was clear that turnout was high in areas with strong support for Le Pen, including in Pas-de-Calais in the north and Picardy, as well as in rural areas where the yellow vest protests on roundabouts began last autumn.

The French far-right election campaign, headed by a slick young candidate from the Paris banlieue, Jordan Bardella, had steadily grown in support since January. Bardella, 23, is set to become one of the youngest ever members of the European parliament.

Le Pen, who took over the far-right party from her father in 2011 and recently changed its name, is experienced at shaping European election campaigns as a national protest vote against those in power - her party also came first in the last European elections in 2014.

Le Pen pitched this campaign as the ultimate protest vote - her party's main message was "Stop Macron" - styling it as a referendum against the centrist young leader whose popularity has slumped.

Le Pen no longer wants France to leave the EU in a so-called Frexit - nor to leave the euro currency. Coming first in the European vote is personally very important for Le Pen because her standing within her party depends on it. She has struggled to recover from a poor and erratic final presidential TV debate against Macron two years ago in the presidential final in 2017. Macron had called the elections "the most important since 1979", warning the EU was facing "an existential risk" from nationalists seeking to divide the bloc.

Coming second does not in theory change Macron's ability to govern at home, where he still has a large parliamentary majority. First, I was thinking it would be fun to just have a discussion thread of The Worst Fat You've Ever Known. Just as a conversation, not necessarily a voting thing (unless others want to do that).

The competition comes in with a regular "Worst Fat of the Month" type conversation. Then, at the end of each month--say on a specific date each month so we don't need to count weeks and such, like maybe the 25th of each month (any entries after that point go into the next month's pool), one thread is posted, or a poll is posted in here (We could also do the first of every month, looking at the previous month's entries). The post would have links to all of the submissions tagged "[Worst Fat]." And people vote on it. The winning entry gets maybe custom flair that rotates to each month's winner (so you only get the custom flair for a month)?

At the end of the year we could do a "Worst Fat of the Year" vote, with links to all the monthly winners.

It could also be expanded into a fat meme-type contest. Obviously if the winner is/contains an image, that could go in the sidebar. But we also have some talented artists here, I know; perhaps someone would be willing to do or find some kind of image that represents the Worst Fat of that month? That might be too difficult to do, and Cars might want to keep those separate; I'm just throwing ideas out there.

Anyway. Like I said, the idea is to increase content and submissions and give us a way to "reward" those who so submit/start threads.

I also keep thinking about the great image of Lord Beetus someone drew for me here very soon after I joined--LB on a Scootypuff with a bag full of feet hanging off the side--and I was thinking that could be an image contest that would be fun: Draw Lord Beetus. Or the poll could just go here in the Weekly OT.

Again, the goal here is to increase participation and bring in more submissions, not just to win contests. That's why I think entries for a "Worst Fat" contest should be regular submissions with just a tag that indicates they'd like to be considered for Worst Fat, rather than a single thread. That way they become just part of the normal conversation here, and people are encouraged to treat them like any other submissions: comment as you would normally, upvoat as you would normally because the number of upvoats doesn't decide who wins. And again, we would discourage comments that just say things like, "This is the winner!" or "Definitely voting for this one." If anyone has any other thoughts about it, please feel free! I came up with the idea but I am in no way possessive or proprietary about it, so I welcome feedback and ideas. I just want to help increase participation here and have something fun for us; I don't care about the purity of my vision or whatever.
